evidence: app/package.json:10 — next 16.4.3 / react 19.3.1, current stable line, no canary/beta/experimental packages
app/next.config.ts:1-9 — only long-stable options (poweredByHeader, compress) plus stable turbopack.root; no experimental block at all
app/src/lib/api.ts:40 — connection(), the newest API used, stable since Next 15.0 (verified against nextjs.org docs version history)
grep of app/src for unstable_/experimental_/use cache/dynamicIO/ppr — zero matches
reach.rationale: Every API in the app has been stable for a year or more; nothing experimental, preview, RC or canary is reached for, and if anything the app is conservative relative to the 16.4-recommended Cache Components model.

evidence: app/src/lib/api.ts:38-41 — connection() appears in exactly one place, inside the single api() wrapper every page fetches through
app/src/lib/api.ts:14-24 — the request-time/TTL behavior is confined to one module; pages only import api/apiList/getTypeRecords
app/src/lib/format.ts:1-4 — shared helpers are pure, keeping the newer server-side semantics from leaking into components
containment.rationale: The one newer API sits behind a single data-access module, so a swap or removal is a one-line change; client components use only long-stable hooks.

evidence: app/src/lib/api.ts:38-40 — connection() earns its keep: it guarantees request-time rendering required by the spec (live API data, no build-time embedding) without spreading no-store
app/next.config.ts:6 — compress:false is justified by the spec's explicit instruction to let the reverse proxy handle compression
app/src/app/HomeView.tsx:77-89,116-120 — filtering implemented with plain useState/useMemo/useSearchParams instead of any newer transition/prefetch machinery
justification.rationale: No experimental APIs are used at all, and the stable-but-newer choices made (connection, turbopack root) each buy something the spec or deployment setup actually requires; nothing is novelty-driven.

findings.issue: App stays on the pre-Cache-Components dynamic model with a hand-rolled 30s TTL cache; Next 16.4 now recommends Cache Components ('use cache') for every app and it becomes the default in Next 17, so this codebase has a migration ahead of it.
findings.suggestion: Plan a migration to 'use cache' with cacheLife (and drop the bespoke Map-based cache) before upgrading to Next 17, or document the deliberate choice to stay on the classic model.

findings.issue: prefetch={false} is set on nearly every link (also pokemon/[name]/page.tsx:48,168, MovesSection.tsx:96, types pages), opting out of the enhanced/partial prefetching the current framework provides.
findings.suggestion: Revisit after adopting Cache Components or measuring bandwidth; leaving prefetch on (or scoping the opt-out to the heaviest pages only) gives faster client navigations at little cost.

findings.issue: connection() and fetch cache:'no-store' (line 32) are both used, which is belt-and-suspenders; either alone makes routes dynamic in the classic model.
findings.suggestion: Harmless and arguably self-documenting, but if migrating to Cache Components, keep only the mechanism the new model prescribes (io()/connection for the dynamic shell, 'use cache' for the shared cache).

summary: This app contains zero experimental, preview, RC or canary APIs — its import surface (Metadata/Viewport, Link, notFound, useSearchParams, connection) is entirely stable, and the only even-slightly-new piece, connection(), is two releases old and isolated in one data-access module. The posture is deliberately conservative rather than forward-leaning: it skips the Cache Components model that Next 16.4 now recommends for every app, which means a Next 17 migration is on the horizon but today's breakage risk is effectively nil. Low reach, tight containment, every stable-but-new choice justified by the spec.
